title: Is Crypto Dead or Still Early? | The Global Council
description:
The Global Council debates whether cryptocurrency is a failed experiment or just getting started.

#Crypto #Bitcoin #Investing #GlobalCouncil #Shorts

segments.text: Bitcoin has been declared dead four hundred and seventy-three times. It keeps coming back. Every cycle, the floor gets higher. We're still early.
The floor gets higher for Bitcoin. Ninety-nine percent of altcoins go to zero. Most people aren't buying Bitcoin. They're buying meme coins and losing everything.
Crypto isn't just coins. It's programmable money. Smart contracts. Decentralized finance. The infrastructure is being built right now.
Infrastructure that nobody uses at scale. Eight years of smart contracts and the killer app is still speculation and money laundering.
Tell that to people in Argentina and Nigeria using stablecoins to escape inflation. Crypto isn't dead. It's just not for privileged economies.

topic: Side Hustles vs Salary: Which Wins?
title: Side Hustles vs Salary: Which Wins? | The Global Council
description:
The Global Council debates whether side income or climbing the corporate ladder is the better path to wealth.

#SideHustle #Salary #Wealth #GlobalCouncil #Shorts

segments.text: A salary has a ceiling. A side hustle has no cap. If you're trading time for money at a job, you'll never build wealth. You need equity in something.
Most side hustles earn less than minimum wage when you factor in all the hours. A six-figure salary with a four-oh-one-k match builds wealth quietly and reliably.
The magic is both. Keep the salary for stability. Use the side hustle for upside. Don't quit your day job until the side income replaces it.
Side hustle culture burns people out. Working eight hours then building a business for four more hours is not a strategy. It's a recipe for collapse.
The real answer is leverage. A salary with no leverage keeps you running. A side hustle that builds an asset gives you options. Choose based on what compounds.

topic: Is Passive Income Real or a Scam?
title: Is Passive Income a Lie? | The Global Council
description:
The Global Council examines whether passive income actually exists or if it's a marketing myth.

#PassiveIncome #Investing #OnlineBusiness #GlobalCouncil #Shorts

segments.text: Dividends. Rental income. Index fund growth. Passive income is real. It's just boring. Nobody makes viral content about slowly getting rich.
Rental income isn't passive. Ask any landlord. And dividends require hundreds of thousands in capital first. Passive income exists, but it's not accessible.
Digital products are the closest to truly passive. Build once, sell forever. My course earns while I sleep. It took six months to build, though.
Every passive income guru is making their real money selling the dream of passive income. The product is the course, not the strategy.
Nothing is fully passive. But there's a spectrum. A job is zero passive. A rental property is seventy percent passive. The goal isn't zero effort. It's decoupling time from income.

topic: Should You Rent or Buy a Home?
title: Rent or Buy in 2026? | The Global Council
description:
The Global Council tackles the housing question with interest rates at historic levels and prices still climbing.

#RentVsBuy #Housing #RealEstate #GlobalCouncil #Shorts

segments.text: At current mortgage rates, buying in most cities costs twice as much as renting the same property. The math doesn't work. Rent and invest the difference.
You're paying someone else's mortgage when you rent. In twenty years, they own an asset. You own receipts. Buying is forced savings.
Forced savings into an illiquid asset with massive transaction costs. If you need to move in five years, you'll lose money to closing costs alone.
The rent versus buy calculation is local. In Austin, rent wins. In Detroit, buying wins. There's no universal answer. Run your numbers.
Home ownership isn't just math. It's stability. Control. Nobody can raise your mortgage payment or refuse to renew your lease. That security has value.

topic: Are Index Funds Still the Best Investment?
title: Are Index Funds Still King? | The Global Council
description:
The Global Council debates whether passive index investing is still the optimal strategy or if the landscape has changed.

#IndexFunds #Investing #SP500 #GlobalCouncil #Shorts

segments.text: The S and P five hundred has returned ten percent annually for a hundred years. No fund manager consistently beats it. Index funds won. The debate is over.
Except the index is now thirty percent tech. You're not diversified. You're making a massive bet on seven companies. That's not what passive investing was designed to be.
Then buy a total market fund. Or add international exposure. The principle is right. Low fees, broad diversification, long time horizon. That hasn't changed.
For most people, yes. But if you have the knowledge and stomach for concentrated bets, individual stocks can dramatically outperform. Most people just shouldn't try.
The real advantage of index funds isn't returns. It's behavior. They remove the temptation to trade. And behavior matters more than performance.

topic: How Much Emergency Fund Is Enough?
title: How Big Should Your Emergency Fund Be? | The Global Council
description:
Three months? Six months? A year? The Global Council debates the right emergency fund size.

#EmergencyFund #PersonalFinance #Savings #GlobalCouncil #Shorts

segments.text: Three to six months of expenses. That's the standard advice and it's standard for a reason. It covers job loss, medical bills, and car repairs.
In this economy? Six months minimum. If you're in tech, make it twelve. Layoffs are taking six to nine months to recover from now.
Having too much in an emergency fund costs you money. Anything beyond six months should be invested. Cash loses value every day to inflation.
It depends on your risk profile. Single income household with kids? You need more. Dual income, no dependents? Three months is plenty.
The amount matters less than the account. High-yield savings earning five percent means your emergency fund is working for you, not just sitting there.

topic: Should You Pay Off Debt or Invest?
title: Pay Off Debt or Invest? | The Global Council
description:
The Global Council tackles the classic personal finance dilemma: eliminate debt first or invest for compound growth?

#DebtFree #Investing #PersonalFinance #GlobalCouncil #Shorts

segments.text: If your debt is above seven percent interest, pay it off first. No investment reliably beats twenty percent credit card interest. Math doesn't lie.
Unless your employer matches your four-oh-one-k. That's a guaranteed one hundred percent return. Always get the match first. Then attack the debt.
The math says invest. The psychology says pay off debt. Being debt-free changes how you think, how you sleep, and what risks you're willing to take.
Do both. The avalanche method on high-interest debt. Minimum payments on low-interest debt. Invest everything else. It's not either or.
The wrong answer is doing neither. Too many people are paralyzed by the question and end up saving nothing and paying minimums. Start somewhere. Today.

topic: Can AI Actually Make You Rich?
title: Can AI Actually Make You Rich? | The Global Council
description:
Everyone's selling the dream of AI wealth. The Global Council separates hype from reality.

#AIMoney #MakeMoneyWithAI #Wealth #GlobalCouncil #Shorts

segments.text: AI is the biggest wealth creation event since the internet. People who learn to use it now are positioning themselves for the next decade. Yes, it can make you rich.
It can make the people who BUILD AI rich. For everyone else, it's a productivity tool. Using ChatGPT doesn't make you an entrepreneur.
The money isn't in using AI. It's in solving problems with AI that people will pay for. Find a painful workflow. Automate it. Charge for it.
I automated my client reporting with AI and saved twenty hours a week. I didn't get rich, but I got my life back. That's worth more than money.
Every AI get-rich-quick video is selling a course, not a strategy. The real money is quiet. It's in boring B2B automation, not flashy prompts.
